title: Emergence Lab, Thomas Medicus, 2015
desc_src: Durch ein Stecksystem aus 216 lasergeschnittenen Acrylglasstreifen wird ein transparentes kubisches Grundgerüst erzeugt. Auf den Flächen dieses Grundgerüstes sind unzählige Bildfragmente aufgemalt, die sich von sechs orthogonal zueinanderstehenden Blickrichtungen zu sechs unterschiedlichen Bildern zusammensetzen. Um störende Spiegelungen innerhalb der Streifen zu vermeiden und das Aussehen eines massiven Glasobjekts zu erzeugen, schwimmt die Skulptur in einem speziellen Silikonöl, das den gleichen Brechungsindex wie Acrylglas besitzt.

title: 윌슨 휘리기그 공원 08 (Whirligig Park, Wilson)
desc_src: The Vollis Simpson Whirliigig Park on Goldsboro Street S. at Douglas Street S. in Wilson, North Carolina, opened on November 2, 2017 to document, conserve, and display the large whirlgigs from Simpson's property in Lucama, North Carolina. Wilson held its first annual Wilson Whirligig Festival in 2004. It was renamed in 2016 to the North Carolina Whirligig Festival, and is usually held the first full weekend of November. The North Carolina legislature named the whirligig the state's official folk art in June 2013.

title: 윌슨 휘리그 파크 14 (Whirligig Park, Wilson, North Carolina 14)
desc_src: The Vollis Simpson Whirliigig Park on Goldsboro Street S. at Douglas Street S. in Wilson, North Carolina, opened on November 2, 2017 to document, conserve, and display the large whirlgigs from Simpson's property in Lucama, North Carolina. Wilson held its first annual Wilson Whirligig Festival in 2004. It was renamed in 2016 to the North Carolina Whirligig Festival, and is usually held the first full weekend of November. The North Carolina legislature named the whirligig the state's official folk art in June 2013.
description_ko: 노스캐롤라이나 윌슨의 공원에 세워진 대형 바람개비형 휘리그 조각들이다. 바람을 받아 회전하는 구조로 설치되어 있다.
detail_text_ko: 이 공원은 2017년 11월 개장했으며, 심슨의 루카마 부지에 있던 대형 휘리그들을 기록·보존·전시하기 위해 조성되었다. 윌슨은 2004년부터 휘리그 축제를 열었고, 2016년 노스캐롤라이나 휘리그 축제로 이름을 바꿨다. 주 의회는 2013년 휘리그를 주의 공식 민속 예술로 지정했다.
notes: 작가명은 원문에 Simpson만 있어 null 처리

attribution: P K / little catastrophes / CC BY 2.0 / via Wikimedia Commons
title: Little catastrophes (5376095974)
desc_src: Dew condenses on a curved glass surface. Some time later one drop becomes too heavy and slides down the curved surface. As it does so it absorbs other dewdrops becoming even heavier. Once a dewdrop starts falling it's downfall is irreversible. How much of our lives is governed by processes that behave in the same manner? = In a chain reaction, positive feedback leads to a self-amplifying chain of events. Cascading failure is ... when one of the elements fails (completely or partially) and shifts its load to nearby elements in the system. Those nearby elements are then pushed beyond their capacity so they become overloaded and shift their load onto other elements. A catastrophic failure is a sudden and total failure of some system from which recovery is impossible. Catastrophic failures often lead to cascading systems failure. Bifurcation theory studies and classifies phenomena characterized by sudden shifts in behavior arising from small changes in circumstances. This may lead to sudden and dramatic changes, for example the unpredictable timing and magnitude of a landslide. en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chain_reaction en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cascading_failure en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catastrophic_failure en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catastrophe_theory

title: '오르간 뱅크' 기계식 저금통, 고양이와 개 ('Organ Bank' Mechanical Coin Bank (Cat and Dog))
artist: 카이저 앤 렉스 사 (Kyser and Rex Company)
desc_src: Cast iron mechanical bank in the shape of an organ with a monkey, dog, and cat on top. To make a deposit, a coin is placed on the tray in the monkey's hand; cranking the lever will then cause the monkey to lower his arm and let the coin slip off tray and into the bank. While this is happening the dog and cat move counter clockwise and bells rings. Manufactured by the Kyser and Rex Company circa 1882. Title: "Organ Bank" Mechanical Coin Bank (Cat and Dog)
description_ko: 오르간 모양의 주철 저금통으로, 위에 앉은 원숭이가 동전을 떨어뜨리면 개와 고양이가 움직이고 종이 울린다.
detail_text_ko: 레버를 돌리면 원숭이가 팔을 내려 쟁반 위의 동전을 떨어뜨린다. 그 동안 개와 고양이가 반시계 방향으로 움직이며 종이 울린다. 원문에 따르면 1882년경 카이저 앤 렉스 사가 제작했다.
notes: artist 필드는 제작사(원문 Manufactured by)

title: 트릭 포니 기계식 저금통 (Trick Pony Mechanical Coin Bank)
desc_src: Cast iron mechanical bank in the shape of a horse near a trough. To operate the bank, a coin is placed in the horse's mouth. Pulling a lever on the side of the bank causes the trough floor to open and lowers the horse's head, allowing the coin to fall through the trough into the bank. Manufactured by the Shepard Hardware Company circa 1885. Title: Trick Pony Mechanical Coin Bank
description_ko: 말 모양 주철 저금통으로, 레버를 당기면 바닥이 열리며 말 머리가 내려가 동전이 통으로 떨어진다.
detail_text_ko: 말 입에 동전을 넣고 옆 레버를 당기면 물통 바닥이 열리고 말 머리가 내려간다. 원문에 따르면 셰퍼드 하드웨어 사가 1885년경 제작했다. 19세기 기계식 저금통의 구동 원리를 보여 주는 장난감이다.
notes: artist 필드 null — 제작사는 원문상 셰퍼드 하드웨어 사
photographer: Peter Adams, Jr. (Designer), Charles G. Shepard (Designer), Shepard Hardware Company (Maker),

title: 아프리카계 미국인 캐리커처 기계식 저금통 (African American Caricature Mechanical Coin Bank)
desc_src: Cast iron mechanical bank in the shape of a bust of an African American man wearing a red shirt and black tie. To operate the bank, a coin is placed in the figure's hand and a lever pressed causing the figure to roll his eyes as the hand deposits the coin in the figure's mouth. Manufactured by the Shepard Hardware Company circa 1883. Title: African American Caricature Mechanical Coin Bank
description_ko: 주철로 만든 흑인 남성 흉상 저금통으로, 레버를 누르면 눈을 굴리며 손의 동전을 입에 넣는다.
detail_text_ko: 붉은 셔츠와 검은 넥타이를 한 흉상의 손에 동전을 올리고 레버를 누르면 눈을 굴리는 동작을 한다. 원문에 따르면 1883년경 셰퍼드 하드웨어 사가 제작했다. 이 작품은 인종을 희화화한 고정관념 이미지를 담고 있어 소개할 때 역사적 맥락을 함께 제시해야 한다.
notes: 인종 희화화 요소 포함 — 게시 전 검토 필요 (통과 처리, 제외 판단은 사람이) [4e 제외: 사람 판단(민감/부적합)]

title: 원숭이와 코코넛 기계식 저금통 (Monkey and Coconut Mechanical Coin Bank)
artist: 제이 앤 이 스티븐스 사 (J and E Stevens Company)
desc_src: Cast iron mechanical bank in the shape of a monkey and a coconut. To make a deposit, a coin is placed in the monkey's right hand. Pushing a lever causes the monkey to drop the coin into the coconut. Manufactured by the J and E Stevens Company circa 1886. Title: Monkey and Coconut Mechanical Coin Bank
description_ko: 원숭이가 쥔 동전을 레버를 밀면 코코넛 속으로 떨어뜨리는 주철 저금통이다.
detail_text_ko: 동전을 원숭이 오른손에 올리고 레버를 밀면 원숭이가 코코넛에 동전을 떨어뜨린다. 원문에 따르면 제이 앤 이 스티븐스 사가 1886년경 제작했다. 19세기 기계식 저금통의 전형적인 구동 방식을 보여 준다.

title: 회전하는 정육면체 움직임 착시 (Spinning cube moving illusion)
desc_src: A spinning cube. NOTE: You'll need a second image to activate this illusion: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Moving_illusion_catalyst.png This image was created by photographing a spinning cube six times during a rotation of 90 degrees. These were then used as scaffoldings for the digitally rendered cubes.
description_ko: 회전하는 정육면체를 이용한 움직임 착시 이미지다. 정지 그림이지만 보완 이미지를 겹치면 움직이는 것처럼 보인다.
detail_text_ko: 원문은 이 착시를 활성화하려면 Wikimedia의 보완 이미지(Moving illusion catalyst)가 필요하다고 밝힌다. 정육면체는 90도 회전하는 동안 여섯 번 찍은 사진을 발판으로 삼아 디지털로 그렸다고 한다. 정지 이미지에서 움직임을 느끼는 옵아트 계열 작품이다.
notes: 보완 이미지 없이는 움직임 확인 불가 — 착시 계열 애매 통과

title: 달리는 말 움직임 착시 (Running horse moving illusion)
desc_src: A moving illusion version of Eadweard Muybridge's galloping horse "movie". NOTE: You'll need a second image to activate this illusion: File:Moving_illusion_catalyst.png This image is not cropped to insure that the effect works properly. Frames used: 1,3,5,7,9 and 11 using https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:The_Horse_in_Motion.jpg . (PD)
description_ko: 에드워드 머이브리지의 질주하는 말 연속 사진을 이용한 움직임 착시 이미지다. 보완 이미지를 겹치면 말이 달리는 것처럼 보인다.
detail_text_ko: 원문은 머이브리지의 말 연속 사진 중 1·3·5·7·9·11번 프레임을 사용했다고 밝힌다. 효과가 나타나려면 보완 이미지(Moving illusion catalyst)가 필요하며, 원본은 효과를 위해 잘리지 않은 상태로 두었다고 한다. 연속 사진의 움직임을 착시로 되살린 광학 장난감 계열이다.
notes: 원작 사진 작가는 머이브리지, 착시 제작자는 미상 — artist null

title: 회전하는 바퀴 움직임 착시 (Spinning wheel moving illusion)
desc_src: Three rings, joined together, spin around. NOTE: You'll need another image for this to work properly: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Moving_illusion_catalyst.png
description_ko: 연결된 고리들이 회전하는 것처럼 보이는 움직임 착시 이미지다. 보완 이미지를 겹쳐야 제대로 작동한다.
detail_text_ko: 원문은 고리들이 함께 연결되어 돈다고 설명하며, 제대로 작동하려면 보완 이미지가 필요하다고 밝힌다. 사진에는 세로 줄무늬가 원형으로 배열된 패턴이 보인다. 정지된 패턴이 회전 착시를 만드는 옵아트 원리를 따른다.
notes: 원문은 세 고리라 하나 이미지는 단일 원형 패턴 — 보완 이미지 필요

title: 풍력 터빈 움직임 착시 (Wind turbine moving illusion)
desc_src: A moving illusion of a wind turbine. NOTE: You'll need a second image to activate this illusion: File:Moving_illusion_catalyst.png
description_ko: 풍력 터빈의 날개가 돌아가는 것처럼 보이는 움직임 착시 이미지다. 보완 이미지를 겹쳐야 효과가 나타난다.
detail_text_ko: 원문은 풍력 터빈의 움직임 착시이며 보완 이미지(Moving illusion catalyst)가 필요하다고 밝힌다. 사진에는 파란 기둥 위 검은 원형 허브에서 줄무늬 날개가 방사형으로 뻗어 있다. 줄무늬 간격의 차이로 회전감을 만드는 광학 장난감 계열이다.
notes: 보완 이미지 필요 — 착시 계열 애매 통과

title: 앞뒤로 움직이는 패턴 착시 (Back and forth)
desc_src: "Frames" move in one directon and squares in another. NOTE: You'll need a second image to activate this illusion: File:Moving_illusion_catalyst.png
description_ko: 프레임은 한 방향으로, 사각형은 다른 방향으로 움직이는 것처럼 보이는 움직임 착시 이미지다.
detail_text_ko: 원문은 프레임과 사각형이 서로 다른 방향으로 움직인다고 설명하며, 보완 이미지(Moving illusion catalyst)를 겹쳐야 한다고 밝힌다. 사진에는 사각형과 줄무늬가 반복되는 패턴이 보인다. 반복 패턴의 엇갈림으로 움직임을 느끼는 옵아트 작품이다.
notes: 보완 이미지 필요 — 착시 계열 애매 통과

title: 스투름글로케 (Sturmglocke)
desc_src: 40 megaphones of different sizes and capacities are fixed to an aluminum grid made in the shape of a bell. All audio inputs are grouped together and connected to one single microphone. The microphone is hanging in the center of the bell just below the megaphones. Only a temporary de-energized system prevents the inevitable audio feedback. As soon as the visitors disturb the microphone from its suspended state, the audio system automatically starts up and the deafening roar of a 40-megaphone chorus of amplified feedback collapses on the bell-ringer.
description_ko: 종 모양 알루미늄 격자에 크기가 다른 메가폰 40여 개를 붙인 사운드 설치다. 관람객이 마이크를 건드리면 증폭된 피드백 굉음이 터진다.
detail_text_ko: 원문에 따르면 모든 오디오 입력은 하나의 마이크로 묶여 있고, 마이크는 종 안쪽 중앙에 매달려 있다. 평소에는 임시로 전원을 끈 상태이며, 방문객이 마이크를 흔들면 시스템이 켜져 메가폰 합창이 울린다. 관람자의 행동이 소리를 깨우는 참여형 사운드 조각이다.

title: Anamorfos 4, Nordisk familjebok
desc_src: Anamorfos (grek. anamorfosis, ombildning), vrängd eller vanskaplig bild, som är ritad på sådant sätt, att den ger riktiga bilder af föremålen, när den betraktas i en viss sned riktning (optisk anamorfos), i en cylindrisk, konisk eller pyramidalisk spegel (katoptrisk a.) eller genom mångkantiga slipade glas (dioptrisk a.). Zeiss i Jena har konstruerat ett linssystem, den s. k. anamorfoten, hvilken, använd som fotografiskt objektiv, möjliggör framställningen af inom önskade gränser förvridna bilder. Fig. 1 visar ett originalmönster. Genom anamorfotens vridning kring sin optiska axel erhållas bilderna fig. 2–4 och mellanformer, alltefter apparatens vridningsgrad. Objektivet är för alla bilderna detsamma och afståndet mellan objekt och bild oförändradt. – Inom botaniken betecknar anamorfos detsamma som tillbakaskridande metamorfos.

attribution: Tom Motblah / Own work / CC BY-SA 4.0 / via Wikimedia Commons
title: Thomas Medicus, Emulsifier, 2014
desc_src: Der "Emulsifier" ist eine handbemalte anamorphe Skulptur, die aus 160 Glasstreifen besteht. Wenn die Installation gedreht wird, erscheint alle 90 Grad eines von vier versteckten Bildern. Das würfelförmige Objekt hat ca. eine Seitenlänge von 35cm.

attribution: Tom Motblah / Own work / CC BY-SA 4.0 / via Wikimedia Commons
title: Human Animal Binary, Thomas Medicus, 2024
desc_src: Die Kunstinstallation Human Animal Binary zeigt vier fragmentierte Abbildungen von in Tirol heimischen Tierarten, die unter dem Einfluss des Klimawandels stehen. Die Bilder von Luchs, Biene, Eisvogel und Bachforelle sind in einem würfelförmigen Raum auf 144 Glasstreifen ineinander verschachtelt angeordnet. Beim Umschreiten der Skulptur lösen sie sich die Darstellungen in Bildfragmente auf und setzen sich wieder zusammen - wie ein ständiges Entstehen und Vergehen der Lebewesen.

desc_src: Speculative Evolution is simulation about a speculative future where technologies like genetic engineering, artificial intelligence and robotics are used to balances our ecosystem. Visitors are invited to create new variations of animals, fungi, plants and robots and to fly with them through a speculative ecosystem from the perspective of AI agents. The project aims to inspect our tendency to simplify complex ecosystems by treating nature as a system that can be fixed.

title: Anamorfos 3, Nordisk familjebok
desc_src: Anamorfos (grek. anamorfosis, ombildning), vrängd eller vanskaplig bild, som är ritad på sådant sätt, att den ger riktiga bilder af föremålen, när den betraktas i en viss sned riktning (optisk anamorfos), i en cylindrisk, konisk eller pyramidalisk spegel (katoptrisk a.) eller genom mångkantiga slipade glas (dioptrisk a.). Zeiss i Jena har konstruerat ett linssystem, den s. k. anamorfoten, hvilken, använd som fotografiskt objektiv, möjliggör framställningen af inom önskade gränser förvridna bilder. Fig. 1 visar ett originalmönster. Genom anamorfotens vridning kring sin optiska axel erhållas bilderna fig. 2–4 och mellanformer, alltefter apparatens vridningsgrad. Objektivet är för alla bilderna detsamma och afståndet mellan objekt och bild oförändradt. – Inom botaniken betecknar anamorfos detsamma som tillbakaskridande metamorfos.
notes: 백과사전 삽화 도안(장식 문양) — 작품 아님

desc_src: At time, I cannot distinguish if it’s me going around the world or it’s the world going around me. Like Hafez, I was on my way to being. Like Attar, I was on my way to Seeking. Like Rumi, I was on my path to finding the sea of seeds. To plant. To water. To will ten commands meant. To reach a certain seeing. Seeing not with my Genital, Libidinal eyes, But as one whom reaches a seeing of a gentiled eyeball. One God. One life. One face. I like to see them faith to faith. Like a Muslim. I a Gentile. Like a Jew. I am a luggage of languages. I am as free as “Bod Ah”. Filed with passionate, pregnant, painful, pomegranate formed pages. Like a Chilled child. Traveling. Going through every one of the cities, the Seven cities of Love. Love the essence God is made out of. Lord the image we were made in two. From our mother’s womb, we were all born through and through and through. Women whom Love us. Us. For the last twenty-seven years I had to explain myself by the way of mouth, telling, telling, I am a pomegranate not a grenade. I am a language. Not a tongue. I am a telling. Not a terrorist. I am a Language of my time. A ticking religion. A Neugier meaning someone nosy in German language. That I am a new. Not a nude. A review. Not a view.

title: The Dock of Deauville
desc_src: This painting treats a common theme in Eugène Boudin's mature art: ships at harbor. Boudin typically did not depict the busy commercial life or human tasks related to ships; rather, he seemed always to strive for an overall mood of calm, harmony, and light. Although Boudin's brushwork was quite sketchy at this time, he was still able to suggest the complex sails and structures of large vessels. Here he rubbed light tones around the ships' masts, often overlapping the darker lines of the wood and rigging with white or gray tones as if to evoke the passing wind and shifting positions common to nautical life.

title: Nathaniel Olds
desc_src: Nathaniel Olds’s glasses have four tinted lenses, two of which are hinged side shields. This style was typically worn to protect sensitive eyes from excessive light, dust, or wind. Due to their occasional use during open-air travel, they were sometimes referred to as carriage or railroad spectacles. The painter of this portrait founded the Western Union Telegraph Company in 1854 and soon became one of Cleveland’s wealthiest industrialists. His grandson, Jeptha Wade II, was a founder of the Cleveland Museum of Art and donated the land upon which it stands as a Christmas gift to the city in 1892.

title: The Beach at Deauville
desc_src: During the 1860s, Boudin executed many paintings and watercolors representing well-to-do tourists and vacationers enjoying seaside resorts in Normandy, principally Trouville and Deauville. In this scene, the informally posed figures suggest a sense of relaxation and intimacy. The overturned chair in the foreground underscores the impression of a casually observed moment, as though a sea breeze or a quick departure by its former occupant has upended it. The majority of Boudin's small oil paintings of beach scenes of the 1860s were executed on wood panel. After laying down a thin white ground, Boudin seems to have begun painting directly, not drawing or laying in guidelines for the forms. The result is a freshness and airiness appropriate to a windy day at the beach.

title: Sentient-gate-joebattleartist
desc_src: "The Sentient Gate Project” This sculpture takes the form of a purely postmodern aesthetic. It works in tandem with technology partners. It is centered on the creation of a shared experience. Reacting to each individual differently, Sensing how each stands within the light, It may react with a gentle sigh or the soft intake of a child’s breath. We feel the impulse to touch its reflective surface. We see our own image reaching towards us. It senses our touch and responds with music or the sound of rain. We are lost in the moment. And for a time viewer and artwork blend in an embrace of the senses. Once a blue bird flew across my field of vision. It landed in the grass in front of me. In the bright sunlight its color was resplendent, and the movements of its flying were flawless. It was in that moment I realized this was the perfect sculpture, one that could interact and react with its environment, one that was also exquisitely made. Why the title "The Sentient Gate"? It is because throughout the centuries sentience has been perceived as a gateway to our Divine nature. How do we define the Divine? It is, after all, that place where consciousness resides. If sentience is our ability to reflect upon our actions, then we must also say that sentience is a path to the Divine. "The Sentient Gate" is a title which attempts to embed the mythology of human thought, regarding the Divine, into the experience of a sculpture.

title: Gardener's House at Antibes
desc_src: In 1888, Claude Monet spent four months in Antibes, a city in southeastern France on the Mediterranean coast, to derive inspiration for painting. Although his visit was occasionally challenged by strong winds that threatened to knock over his easel, the artist was able to complete nearly 40 works. This especially vibrant canvas is a depiction of a gardener’s house set against the sea and the distant Alps. Monet portrays intense midday light through thickly applied paint in bright colors that evoke the region’s sun-drenched climate. Small daubs of green on the slender trees framing the house suggest the onset of spring.
notes: 정원·풍경 유화 — 일반 회화

title: Winding Yarn (Interior of a Nantucket Kitchen)
desc_src: Set in a rustic kitchen on Nantucket Island, Massachusetts, this painting depicts a woman who winds a ball of yarn from a coil looped in the hands of a man sitting across from her at a respectable distance. At the time, winding yarn was a common symbol of courtship that carried humorous overtones of a woman ensnaring her suitor. The second woman in the composition is likely a chaperone. The suitor’s unrefined, open-legged pose, coupled with his rude action of placing his hat on the floor, adds further comic elements that contemporary audiences would have appreciated.

title: 바람 앞에 서다 (Recht op de wind)

detail_text_ko: 원문은 네덜란드 트리흐트(Tricht) 마을의 회오리바람 기념물이며 마르쿠스 라번스바이의 작품이라고 밝힌다. 인물들이 위로 뒤틀리며 올라가는 자세가 회오리 움직임을 연상시킨다.

title: 프락시노스코프 극장 (Praxinoscopio teatro)
desc_src: Praxinoscopio teatro en Mar del Plata, Argentina
description_ko: 회전하는 원통 안의 거울에 그림 인물이 움직이는 것처럼 보이게 하는 광학 장난감이다.
detail_text_ko: 아르헨티나 마르델플라타에서 촬영된 프락시노스코프 극장이다. 원통 안쪽의 그림 띠가 회전하면 가운데 거울 면에 비친 인물들이 움직이는 것처럼 보인다. 원문에는 제작 연도와 작가가 없다.
notes: 중복후보: 2882 (같은 기구의 다른 사진)

attribution: Stef Rae / Own work / CC BY-SA 4.0 / via Wikimedia Commons
title: 볼리스 심슨 휠리직 공원 (Vollis Simpson Whirligig Park)
desc_src: Simpson's whirligigs high in the air at the future Vollis Simpson Whirligig Park.
description_ko: 바람에 회전하는 대형 금속 휠리직 조각들이 설치된 공원이다.
detail_text_ko: 원문은 볼리스 심슨 휠리직 공원의 휠리직(바람 회전 조각)을 촬영한 것이라고 밝힌다. 사진에는 높은 기둥과 바퀴 형태의 금속 부품들이 공중에 설치된 모습이 보인다. 제작 연도는 원문에서 확인되지 않는다.
notes: 제작연도 미확인; 촬영연도(2016)는 제작연도로 쓰지 않음

attribution: Vindlys / Own work / CC BY-SA 4.0 / via Wikimedia Commons
title: 에도 풍령 (Edo-Hurin)
desc_src: Edo-Hurin (Edo style wind chime). On 20 Jul 2017. At Kawasaki-Daishi.
description_ko: 에도 양식의 유리 풍령들이 줄에 매달려 있다. 바람이 불면 흔들려 소리를 내는 구조다.
detail_text_ko: 가와사키 다이시 일대에서 판매되는 일본 전통 풍령을 촬영한 사진이다. 얇은 유리 구체 안쪽에 채색 무늬가 있고 아래쪽에는 종이 장식이 달려 있다. 작가와 제작 연도는 원문에서 확인되지 않는다. 바람을 받아 움직이며 소리를 내는 점이 감상 포인트다.
notes: 사진은 판매 진열 상태로 보여 실제 작동 여부는 확인되지 않음

attribution: Luis Miguel Bugallo Sánchez (Lmbuga) / Own work / CC BY-SA 4.0 / via Wikimedia Commons
title: 소타벤토 12 (Sotavento 12)
desc_src: Weather vane, Sotavento, Xermade, Galicia (Spain).
description_ko: 비행기 형태의 풍향계가 기둥 끝에 얹혀 바람 방향에 따라 회전하는 구조다.
detail_text_ko: 스페인 갈리시아 지방 소타벤토 일대 들판에 설치된 야외 풍향계 조각이다. 색이 다른 여러 기둥 위에 비행기 모양 날개가 놓여 있다. 작가 정보는 원문에서 확인되지 않는다. 바람을 받아 돌아가는 구조와 들판 풍경이 어우러지는 점이 감상 포인트다.

title: 트리니타티스 교회 풍향계 (Weather vane Trinitatis kirke)
desc_src: The weather vane of the Trinitatis kirke, as seen from the Rundetårn, Copenhagen, Denmark.
description_ko: 왕관과 문양으로 장식된 풍향계가 교회 첨탑 위에서 바람 방향을 가리킨다.
detail_text_ko: 덴마크 코펜하겐 트리니타티스 교회 첨탑 위에 설치된 풍향계다. 왕관 장식과 덩굴형 문양이 달려 있고 푸른 하늘을 배경으로 촬영되었다. 작가와 제작 연도는 원문에서 확인되지 않는다. 바람 방향에 따라 회전하는 구조이지만 장식성이 강해 키네틱 작품으로 보기에는 애매하다.
notes: 건물 첨탑 장식 성격이 강함. 작품 성격 판단 보류, 사람 검토 권장

attribution: Nikolai Bulykin / Own work / CC BY-SA 4.0 / via Wikimedia Commons
title: 바이코누르 우주기지 풍향계 (Космодром Байконур, флюгер на Гагаринском старте)
desc_src: Plane-looking weather vane at Baikonur Cosmodrome Site 1. Kyzylorda Region, Kazakhstan.
description_ko: 비행기 모양의 풍향계가 기둥 위에 얹혀 바람 방향에 따라 돌아가는 구조다.
detail_text_ko: 카자흐스탄 바이코누르 우주기지 1번 부지에 설치된 비행기 형태 풍향계를 촬영한 사진이다. 원문 제목에 따르면 가가린 발사대 인근이다. 금속 벽면을 배경으로 기둥 위에 놓여 있다. 작가와 제작 연도는 원문에서 확인되지 않는다. 장소성과 바람 구동 구조가 함께 드러나는 점이 감상 포인트다.
notes: 작가 미상, 설치 연도 원문 미확인

attribution: Mostafameraji / Own work / CC BY-SA 4.0 / via Wikimedia Commons
title: 사자 풍향계 (Tbilisi, Georgian)
desc_src: Weather vane on a restaurant at Akaki Bakradze Street in Tbilisi (called Avalon in 2016, München as of 2025)
description_ko: 사자 실루엣과 방위 표시가 달린 풍향계가 뾰족한 지붕 위에서 바람을 가리킨다.
detail_text_ko: 조지아 트빌리시의 한 건물 지붕 위에 설치된 풍향계를 촬영한 사진이다. 사자 형상의 실루엣과 방위 문자, 화살표가 달려 있으며 푸른 하늘 아래 놓여 있다. 작가와 제작 연도는 원문에서 확인되지 않는다. 바람 방향에 따라 회전하는 구조이지만 장식적 성격이 강하다.
notes: 장식 위주 풍향계로 작품성 판단 보류

title: 뿌리와 가지 (Roots and Branches) 02 — 연주 기타
desc_src: Part of the amazing sculpture that plays the instruments to produce a haunting random melody.
description_ko: 모터가 기타를 구동해 연주하는 기계식 조각의 일부다.
detail_text_ko: 「Roots and Branches」 조각의 한 부분으로, 파란 기타에 모터와 금속 프레임이 연결되어 있다. 원문에 따르면 이 조각은 악기를 연주해 무작위 멜로디를 만든다. 작가 정보는 원문에서 확인되지 않는다. 기계 장치가 악기를 직접 움직여 음악을 만드는 점이 감상 포인트다.

title: 뿌리와 가지 (Roots and Branches) 04 — 불협화음 화음
desc_src: Part of the amazing sculpture that plays the instruments to produce a haunting random melody.
description_ko: 여러 기타와 악기가 빽빽하게 엮인 기계식 조각의 일부로, 악기를 연주해 음을 만든다.
detail_text_ko: 「Roots and Branches」 조각의 한 부분으로, 기타 넥과 몸통, 드럼, 밴조가 겹쳐 배열되어 있다. 원문은 이 조각이 악기를 연주해 무작위 멜로디를 만든다고 설명한다. 사진에서는 구동 장치가 뚜렷하지 않아 움직임 자체는 확인되지 않는다. 작가 정보는 원문에서 확인되지 않는다.
notes: 구동 장치가 사진에서 보이지 않음(원문 설명 근거). 중복후보: 1628, 1640 [4e 중복정리: 1628 와 같은 작품]

title: 헨리 베르토이아의 소리 조각 (Sounding Sculptures, Chicago)
desc_src: Henry Bertoia, Sounding Sculptures, Chicago
description_ko: 헨리 베르토이아의 소리 조각으로, 가늘고 긴 금속 봉이 촘촘하게 세워져 있다.
detail_text_ko: 원문 제목에 따르면 시카고에 설치된 헨리 베르토이아의 「Sounding Sculptures」 계열 작품이다. 가늘고 긴 청동색 금속 봉이 수직으로 빽빽하게 세워져 있고, 고층 건물과 나무를 배경으로 놓여 있다. 사진만으로는 봉이 흔들리거나 소리를 내는 장면이 확인되지 않는다. 제작 연도는 원문에서 확인되지 않는다.

year_raw: Taken on 23 October 2023, 12:25:00 (according to Exif data)

description_ko: 바람을 받아 돌아가도록 만든 프로펠러형 바람 장난감으로, 아치 아래 설치되어 있다.
detail_text_ko: 원문에 따르면 뮌헨 장난감박물관(Spielzeugmuseum)과 관련된 바람 장난감을 촬영한 사진이다. 여러 날개를 가진 프로펠러가 금속 막대 끝에 달려 있으며, 뒤로 뮌헨 신시청사와 프라우엔 성당의 탑이 보인다. 작가와 제작 연도는 원문에서 확인되지 않는다. 바람을 받아 회전하는 구조가 감상 포인트다.

title: 태엽 장난감 관람차 (Clockwork Tin Toy Ferris Wheel)
desc_src: Clockwork mechanical tin toy Ferris wheel. Title: Clockwork Tin Toy Ferris Wheel
description_ko: 태엽 기계 장치로 돌아가는 양철 관람차 장난감으로, 인형들이 칸에 앉아 함께 회전한다.
detail_text_ko: 태엽식 기계로 작동하는 양철 장난감 관람차다. 붉은 지붕 아래 금속 골조에 칸이 달려 있고 인형들이 앉아 있다. 측면의 손잡이와 태엽 장치가 구동부로 보인다. 제작자와 제작 연도는 원문에서 확인되지 않는다. 기계 장치로 움직이는 오토마타형 장난감이라는 점이 감상 포인트다.

title: La Cervara, the Roman Campagna
desc_src: Corot based his large oil painting on drawings and oil sketches made outdoors. Attracted to the beauty of the Italian countryside, he often sketched around Rome, where he lived from 1825 to 1828. This painting's highly structured composition, based on forms moving into the distance along a series of diagonals, is characteristic of Corot's early style and recalls the classical landscapes of 17th-century painter Nicholas Poussin.

title: Low Waterfall in a Wooded Landscape with a Dead Beech Tree
desc_src: Jutting from a dune in the foreground, the massive silvery trunk of a dead tree leads the eye across a waterfall and toward a distant sunlit field where travelers and a dog traverse a sandy path. Partly masked by trees, a ruined building is turned gold by the sun. In Jacob van Ruisdael’s landscapes, dead trees, waterfalls, and ruined buildings were visual expressions of the passage of time. Ruisdael devoted equal attention to the cloud-filled skies looming above the land, creating dramatic patterns of light and shadow and revealing the unseen movements of the wind.
notes: 풍경 회화(Ruisdael 계열) — 정적 회화

desc_src: Cast iron mechanical bank. Depicts two African American boys stealing watermelons from a field guarded by a dog in a doghouse. To make a deposit, a coin is placed in the slot on top of the dog house. Pushing a lever moves the dog out of the house allowing the coin to fall. The action also animates the boys' arms. Manufactured by the Kyser and Rex Company from 1885 to 1895. Title: Boys Stealing Watermelons Mechanical Coin Bank
description_ko: 레버를 밀면 밭을 지키던 개가 개집에서 나오며 동전이 떨어지고, 소년들의 팔이 함께 움직이는 기계식 저금통이다.
detail_text_ko: 원문에 따르면 Kyser and Rex Company가 1885년에서 1895년 사이 제작한 주철 저금통이다. 동전을 개집 위 구멍에 넣고 레버를 누르면 개가 밖으로 나오면서 동전이 아래로 떨어지고 소년들의 팔도 함께 움직인다. 당시의 인물 묘사를 담고 있어 감상 시 제작 시대의 맥락을 함께 고려할 필요가 있다.

title: The Healing of Tobit
desc_src: This scene is the moving conclusion of the story of Tobias, the young man at the right. It addresses the themes of family devotion and trust. Tobias’s father sent him on a long journey to retrieve family money. The angel Raphael appeared as a relative, offering the traveler protection against such things as an attack by a huge fish, whose organs Tobias took on Raphael’s advice. Upon his return home, Tobias discovers his father has gone blind, and Raphael advises him to place the fish’s gallbladder on his father’s eyes to cure him. Strozzi depicts the miraculous cure and the moment in which Raphael reveals that he is an angel.
notes: 종교·역사 회화(Strozzi 계열) — 정적 회화

title: Night Café
desc_src: Following Cubist principles, this painting depicts a table from multiple perspectives, providing different views of various objects simultaneously. Louis Casimir Ladislas Markus was born in Warsaw, Poland, into a Jewish family that had converted to Catholicism. In 1903, he moved to Paris where he met poet Guillaume Apollinaire and artists Georges Braque and Pablo Picasso. He then began experimenting with Cubism. Also of Polish descent, Apollinaire had changed his own name and urged the artist to change his name to Marcoussis after a French village. The yellow hot air balloon and the French flag glimpsed out of the window pay homage to the artist’s adopted homeland.
notes: 입체주의 정물화 — 일반 회화

title: Polychromatic far-field interferometer
desc_src: An x-ray far-field interferometer using only phase gratings is based on the phase moiré effect. The mid grating forms Fourier images of the first grating. These images beat with the 3rd grating to produce broad moiré fringes on the detector at the appropriate distance. Phase shifts and de-coherence of the wavefront by the object cause fringe shifts and attenuation of the fringe contrast.

title: Globe Sewing Table (Globustisch)
materials_raw: Burl walnut veneer, mahogany, ebony, satinwood, gilt wood, painted wood; mirrored glass; metal
desc_src: Work tables resembling globes were the usual form for a lady's sewing or writing table around 1800 in Austria. Combining moving parts, secret compartments, and highly finished decoration, these tables were also a way for the cabinetmaker to show off his skill. The tripod supports and temple-like architectural quality of both the exterior and interior decoration reflect the fashionable taste for neoclassical style, or Biedermeier as it was called in Austria, where Vienna was the center of such elaborate furniture production.
materials: Burl walnut veneer, mahogany, ebony, satinwood, gilt wood, painted wood; mirrored glass; metal

title: OBMOKhU 제2차 봄 전시 전경, 모스크바 (View of Second Spring Exhibition of the OBMOKhU)
desc_src: View of Second Spring Exhibition of the OBMOKhU . Bolshaia Dimitrovska, Moscow, 1921. In 1921 the Constructivists expressed their ideas at an ambitious Moscow exhibition under the umbrella of the Society of Young Artists ( Общество молодых художников abbreviated to ОБМОХУ/OBMOKhU, OBMOChU ). Johannsons' nine three-dimensional space structures , "self-stressed constructions", exhibited innovative tension-integrity strain-stress principles of tensegrity .
description_ko: 1921년 모스크바 OBMOKhU 전시에서 구성주의자들이 선보인 입체 공간 구조물의 전시 장면이다.
detail_text_ko: 원문에 따르면 1921년 구성주의자들이 OBMOKhU 제2차 봄 전시에서 텐세그리티(인장과 압축의 균형) 원리를 적용한 공간 구조물을 발표했다. 사진에는 철사와 막대로 짠 구조물과 상부에 매달린 고리 형태가 보인다. 구조물 자체는 정적이어서 움직임 여부는 확인되지 않아 불확실 표시를 붙인다.

title: Anamorfos 2, Nordisk familjebok
desc_src: Anamorfos (grek. anamorfosis, ombildning), vrängd eller vanskaplig bild, som är ritad på sådant sätt, att den ger riktiga bilder af föremålen, när den betraktas i en viss sned riktning (optisk anamorfos), i en cylindrisk, konisk eller pyramidalisk spegel (katoptrisk a.) eller genom mångkantiga slipade glas (dioptrisk a.). Zeiss i Jena har konstruerat ett linssystem, den s. k. anamorfoten, hvilken, använd som fotografiskt objektiv, möjliggör framställningen af inom önskade gränser förvridna bilder. Fig. 1 visar ett originalmönster. Genom anamorfotens vridning kring sin optiska axel erhållas bilderna fig. 2–4 och mellanformer, alltefter apparatens vridningsgrad. Objektivet är för alla bilderna detsamma och afståndet mellan objekt och bild oförändradt. – Inom botaniken betecknar anamorfos detsamma som tillbakaskridande metamorfos.

title: Flowers in a Vase
desc_src: With just a few flowers, Verelst created a composition of great sophistication and balance. A simple glass flask is filled with a large rose, a red anemone, and a white narcissus tinged with pink. These flowers are surrounded by a scattering of smaller blossoms. Like many still-life painters, Verelst depicted a window reflected in the glass vase, but here he did not show the window's precise structure. He did, however, use another common device: the depiction of a few chips in the stone surface to make the material seem more tangible. Early in his career, Verelst moved from Holland to London, where he worked for the court of King James II and was extravagantly praised for the realism of his flower paintings.

title: Rishabha, the First Jina
desc_src: According to Jain tenets, Rishabha was the first of the 24 Jinas of our current world cycle and is the only one depicted with long locks of hair. He had been a king who was moved to seek an end to the cruel cycles of birth and death after witnessing a dancer die at his court in mid performance. As part of his act of renunciation, he pulled his hair out by handfuls, but the king of the gods interceded before he was finished; some long locks remain as his distinguishing feature. Indian sculpture during the medieval period (700s-1200s) is characterized by linear stylization, as seen here in the high arch of the eyebrows and deeply upturned corners of the mouth. During this time Jinas, like Buddhas, were depicted with the protuberance atop the head as an indicator of enlightenment.

title: Sleeping Endymion
desc_src: Cornacchini moved away from the dramatic movement and light effects characteristic of baroque sculpture toward a calmer, gentler, more graceful style favored by 18th-century taste. This sculpture depicts Endymion, a beautiful young shepherd from Greek mythology. His beauty so entranced Selene, the personification of the moon, that she asked Zeus to grant Endymion immortality. Zeus did so, but only after placing Endymion in an eternal sleep.

desc_src: Work tables resembling globes were the usual form for a lady's sewing or writing table around 1800 in Austria. Combining moving parts, secret compartments, and highly finished decoration, these tables were also a way for the cabinetmaker to show off his skill. The tripod supports and temple-like architectural quality of both the exterior and interior decoration reflect the fashionable taste for neoclassical style, or Biedermeier as it was called in Austria, where Vienna was the center of such elaborate furniture production.

title: Panel: Spring

desc_src: Courtiers and aristocrats anxious to model their lifestyles on the king also commissioned works from the same state manufactories that produced tapestries, carpets, and upholstery for the French monarchy. Established in the early 1600s, the Savonnerie factory provided both domestic furnishings for the king’s palaces and diplomatic gifts for foreign heads of state. The double coat of arms in this tapestry suggests that it was made for a count and countess who married in 1717. One of a group of four tapestries depicting the seasons, this work depicts the abundant flora and fauna of spring. The Cleveland Museum of Art rotates this tapestry with another from this group. title: Pair of Boots
materials_raw: Silk: tapestry weave; two kinds of metal threads
desc_src: This magnificent pair of boots, made of finely woven silk tapestry (kesi), features two phoenixes in flight chasing a flaming pearl. Although the bright colors of the fabric have become muted from being buried in a tomb and the gold threads are partly disintegrated, the once lavish use of gold and the Chinese-inspired phoenix motif suggest that the boots were made for a member of the Liao imperial family, probably a woman. At the time the boots were made in the Khitan-occupied territory in northern China, footbinding was introduced among upper-class women in southern China. The high value the Khitan people accorded to boots relates to their mobile, seminomadic lifestyle.
materials: Silk: tapestry weave; two kinds of metal threads

desc_src: Instead of a "prick" terminus at the neck, the rowel spur had a rotating wheel installed between two prongs. title: Pricked Spur
desc_src: The spur was an essential part of the knight's equipment. Fastened to his heels by means of straps and buckles, it was used to prod a horse into action. This example represents the oldest type recorded, the "pricked" spur, so-called because its neck terminated in a spike. The pricked spur was replaced during the Middle Ages by the "rowel" spur, with a rotating spiked wheel.
notes: 박차(정적 금속 공예품)

title: Anamorfos 1, Nordisk familjebok
desc_src: Anamorfos (grek. anamorfosis, ombildning), vrängd eller vanskaplig bild, som är ritad på sådant sätt, att den ger riktiga bilder af föremålen, när den betraktas i en viss sned riktning (optisk anamorfos), i en cylindrisk, konisk eller pyramidalisk spegel (katoptrisk a.) eller genom mångkantiga slipade glas (dioptrisk a.). Zeiss i Jena har konstruerat ett linssystem, den s. k. anamorfoten, hvilken, använd som fotografiskt objektiv, möjliggör framställningen af inom önskade gränser förvridna bilder. Fig. 1 visar ett originalmönster. Genom anamorfotens vridning kring sin optiska axel erhållas bilderna fig. 2–4 och mellanformer, alltefter apparatens vridningsgrad. Objektivet är för alla bilderna detsamma och afståndet mellan objekt och bild oförändradt. – Inom botaniken betecknar anamorfos detsamma som tillbakaskridande metamorfos.

title: TV Bot - World News as Soon as It Happens, Port25, Mannheim, Marc Lee
desc_src: The TV Bot is an Internet news channel which only broadcasts brand new stories. Never more than an hour old, they are scooped from the Internet’s news flux, reformatted for a browser and given a URL. The process is automated, with no editorial hand behind the content selection which is reproduced in apparently random order as live TV streams, live radio streams, webcam images and text-based headlines. The only criterion that matters is “liveness”. In its graphical representation, TV Bot makes obvious reference to well-known international TV broadcasters like CNN and n-tv. By being more live than these TV channels, Marc Lee interrogates the informativeness of broadcasters that are permanently oriented to up-to-dateness and audience numbers. The Swiss media artist, who also works with installation, largely focuses on the Internet and its structures. Also active as a software developer, Lee breaks open the mechanisms of the World Wide Web, revealing them to ordinary users and enabling critical reflection. The TV Bot is an ironic challenge to our media society’s “real time” dogma. http://marclee.io/en/tv-bot-world-news-as-soon-as-it-happens/

title: A Cottage in the Woods
desc_src: Inspired by the native Dutch landscape, Meindert Hobbema specialized in scenes of dense forest growth punctured by winding paths and views toward sunlit clearings that beckon with fertile fields and rustic cottages. Hobbema’s paintings were especially popular among Dutch citizens, who took enormous pride in their land. In addition to nationalistic pride in having recently gained independence from Spain, there was also a profound awareness of the preciousness of land in a low-lying nation, which required dikes, pumps, and constant vigilance to guard against flooding. While the Dutch earned much of their considerable wealth from sea trade, agriculture and livestock were important sources of prosperity.

title: Concealed Drawer for a Globe Work Table (Globustisch)
materials_raw: Burl walnut veneer, mahogany, ebony, satinwood, gilt wood, painted wood
desc_src: Work tables resembling globes were the usual form for a lady's sewing or writing table around 1800 in Austria. Combining moving parts, secret compartments, and highly finished decoration, these tables were also a way for the cabinetmaker to show off his skill. The tripod supports and temple-like architectural quality of both the exterior and interior decoration reflect the fashionable taste for neoclassical style, or Biedermeier as it was called in Austria, where Vienna was the center of such elaborate furniture production.
materials: Burl walnut veneer, mahogany, ebony, satinwood, gilt wood, painted wood

title: Shiva and Parvati
desc_src: Bronze sculptures made during the Chola period (800s–1200s) are among the most celebrated and popular art forms of the Indian tradition. The sensual renditions of attenuated, youthful, and athletic forms are barely covered by garments and ornaments that move, yet cling to the bodies. The figures stand with a natural ease, and the volumes have been so skillfully rendered by the artists that they appear to be capable of walking the earth. Their serene and smiling expressions are completely idealized, leaving no mistake that these are gods, not humans.

title: The Angel of the Ninth Sphere (from the Tarocchi, series A:  Firmaments of the Universe, #49)
desc_src:
This engraving is part of the Tarocchi group marked with the letter “A”, and named Firmaments of the Universe. This series comprises the seven planets from the classical astronomy (Moon, Mercury, Venus, Sun, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn) and the three celestial spheres that separate them from the Supreme Entity (Prima Causa) from which everything was originated.

Here, Primo Mobile (Prime Mover or the Angel of the Ninth Sphere) is personified as a full-length angel, turned to left, and holding up a large sphere in its hands while only standing on its left foot. The Prime Mover corresponds to the ninth and last of the material spheres, beyond the region of the fixed starts. It was believed to be crystalline and invisible, as well as in direct contact with the First Cause—God himself—from which it takes its infinite speed. Thus, it is here shown as an empty disc held by an angel in a dancing pose.
notes: Tarocchi 판화(Primo Mobile 천사) — 정적 판화/회화

title: Gluttony (Land of Cockaigne)
desc_src: This copperplate was engraved with a lozenge-section burin in Antwerp (in present-day Belgium)—an important center for print publishing—in the 1560s. The subject is an imaginary land of ease and luxury, where food falls from trees (the Land of Cockaigne, or Luilekkerland in Dutch).  To engrave, a copperplate is balanced on a sandbag. The sandbag allows the engraver to adjust the plate’s position while slowly guiding the burin to remove the copper. Rather than moving the hand in a pushing motion, the engraver forces the copperplate into the tool, rotating or tilting on the sandbag as necessary, while keeping the hand relatively still.
notes: 16세기 동판 판화 — 정적 판화, 움직임 없음

title: Statuette of a Reclining Woman
desc_src: This tiny statuette is made from amber, or fossilized tree sap. A nude woman reclines against a rocky feature, surrounded by sumptuous piles of fabric which wind around her right arm and leg. Her gaze is upturned, loose hair framing her face. There are cracks throughout the figure, and she is missing both hands and some of her face. She may represent a nymph or maenad.

desc_src: This sculpture of the Hindu god Vishnu once had four arms, indicating his superhuman power. The scarf tied loosely around his hips curves gracefully under its own weight, emphasizing his passive immobility, since it would come undone if he were to move.

title: Head of Sekhmet
desc_src: This lioness head once belonged to a grand statue of the goddess Sekhmet, "the powerful one," probably seated and wearing a tight dress. Possibly appealing to her healing aspect, Pharaoh Amenhotep III, often described as “beloved of Sekhmet,” commissioned and dedicated hundreds of large granodiorite Sekhmet sculptures in his Theban mortuary temple. Thus, this head likely comes from Thebes, perhaps later moved across the Nile—like many such sculptures—to the temple of Mut, a related deity, at Karnak. Behind her stylized ruff, Sekhmet wears a wig, once crowned with a sun disk and uraeus, the stylized cobra symbolizing royal or divine power.
notes: 고대 이집트 사자머리 석조 조각 — 정적 조각

title: Peasants Crossing a Stream
desc_src: The painting is characteristic of Jan Siberechts's Antwerp style, characterized by scenes with fords through which peasants wade with their cattle. The peasants wear simple but brightly colored attire and stand out against the cool green landscape. Flanked by overgrown foliage, the silver hues of the still stream shimmer with reflections. Over the course of his career, which included moving to London in 1672, Siberechts continued to use many of the same figures in his paintings, including Flemish peasant women carrying jugs, like the one seen in this painting. Likewise, his approaches to depicting animals, such as the cows seen here, changed very little over time and are ubiquitous throughout his oeuvre.
notes: 17세기 유화 풍경·인물화 — 일반 회화

title: Nine Celestial Bodies (Navagraha)
desc_src: Near temple entrances, the nine celestial bodies were depicted in an orderly row, often in figural form. From left to right they are: Sun with a tall crown and the female Dawn in front of him. The next five figures are nearly identical: Moon, Mercury, Venus, Mars, and Jupiter. As a portent of doom, Saturn was wounded by a goddess to prevent him from moving swiftly, so he stands on one leg. The bodiless head is Rahu, the eclipse, who swallows the moon until it falls out his neck. The serpent-tailed figure is a comet.
notes: 사암 부조(나바그라하 9행성) — 정적 조각

detail_text_ko: 원문은 Newton on the Moor 마을회관에 설치된 풍향계라고 설명한다. 이미지에서 화살 모양 바람개비와 W·E 방위 표시가 확인된다. 기능성 장치이면서 바람에 반응해 움직이는 점에서 키네틱 요소를 가진다.

title: 빈드하크 날씨 셔틀 (Wettershuttle)
desc_src: Windhaag bei Freistadt: Wettershuttle, 1999 von Gerhard Eilmsteiner (* 1953) (Beschreibung der Gemeinde: [1] )
description_ko: 빈드하크 마을에 있는 1999년작 '날씨 셔틀' 조형물로, 벽 위의 바퀴와 원반형 부품이 움직이는 구조다.
detail_text_ko: 원문은 빈드하크 바이 프라이슈타트(Windhaag bei Freistadt) 마을 소개에 실린 설명으로, 1999년 게르하르트 아일름슈타이너(1953년생)가 제작했다고 적혀 있다. 이미지에서는 붉은 테두리 바퀴와 원반형 부품이 레일 위에 얹힌 모습이 확인된다. 구동 방식은 원문에 없어 확인하지 못했다.
notes: 구동 방식 이미지로 확정 불가

detail_text_ko: 원문은 바람 부는 날 방문했더니 예상보다 조용했다는 방문 감상 한 줄뿐이다. 제작자와 설치 연도는 원문에 없다. 이미지에서는 다양한 길이의 파이프가 바람에 열린 구조로 배열되어 있다. 바람에 반응해 소리를 내는 구조가 감상 포인트다.
notes: 원문 정보가 빈약함 (작가·연도 미확인) [4e 중복정리: 1645 와 같은 작품]
